title: 5.56mm Rifle Ammunition for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police has a requirement to purchase 5.56mm ammunition from FBI contract number 15F06721D0002625 which is a mandatory contract according to COTI 143.08-02. title: Abrasive Blasting and New Paint for USPP NYFO Marine Patrol Unit Vessels
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) Marine Patrol Unit (MPU) has a requirement to perform abrasive blasting to two MPU marine vessels to remove old paint, barnacles, rust, and contaminants from their hulls and then repaint the hulls with new paint. title: Acquisition of Additional Canine Working Dogs and Training for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police has a requirement to acquire additional canine working dogs and training for the US Park Police Canine Unit. The USPP Canine Unit requires additional patrol dogs that are trained and skilled in tracking, handler protection, off-leash obedience, criminal apprehension, and article, area and building search. This is an Administrative Priority.

title: Additional Trunked Radio Channels for USPP NYFO
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) has a requirement to add two trunked radio channels to the USPP radio system. A trunked radio system is a sophisticated, computer-controlled radio network that efficiently manages a pool of shared radio frequencies among many user groups by dynamically assigning channels. These trunked channels will add these trunked channels to the radio workstations in the USPP NYFO Dispatch Center.

title: All Terrain Vehicle (ATV) for the USPP NYFO
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) has a requirement for two All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs) with police equipment for the Jamaica Bay Unit (JBU) located on Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn.

title: All Terrain Vehicle (ATV) for the USPP WMA HMP Unit
description: The US Park Police Horse Mounted Patrol (HMP) Unit in Washington, DC has a requirement for an All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) to accommodate moving hay, sawdust, feed, barn supplies, shuttling personnel and equipment, and to assist in the cleaning of horse manure from the streets.

title: CCTV / Video Surveillance System (VSS) for the USPP Anacostia Operations Facility (AOF)
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement for lifecycle replacement of the CCTV / Video Surveillance System (VSS) at its Anacostia Operations Facility (AOF). The current VSS is outdated and no longer meets the operational, technical, or compliance requirements of a Level 3 facility as defined by the ISC. Requirement is dependent upon final decisions/funding regarding the construction/rehab of USPP facilities from funds provided thru EO 14333.

title: CCTV Cameras at Fort Washington Park (FOWA)
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) has a requirement for the purchase and installation of at least four CCTV surveillance cameras to provide day and night surveillance at the Fort Washington Park (FOWA). FOWA is no longer monitored by NPS guard force personnel. Two cameras at each entrance are necessary to record vehicles entering and exiting FOWA.

title: DC Dispatch Operations Center AIS Software Upgrade for P25 Integration
description: The USPP DC Dispatch Operations Center has a requirement to upgrade its existing AIS Software for mandatory P25 law enforcement radio integration.

title: DC Dispatch Operations Center Desktop Computer Replacement
description: All the USPP Dispatch Operations Centers (DC, NYFO, and SFFO) have a requirement to upgrade their existing desktop computers. The recent deployment of the new Mark 43 Law Enforcement Resource Management System (RMS) requires additional RAM and processing speed than what exists in the current outdated desktops being used in the USPP Dispatch Operations Center.

title: Electronic Citation Warning System for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement to purchase an Electronic Citation Warning System (ECWS) and mobile printers to begin using e-Citation technology available to USPP personnel through the Mark 43 System. ECWS is designed to streamline the process of issuing citations through electronic printing, data collection, and integration which will increase operational accuracy and efficiency and safety on the roads.

title: Evidence Tracker (E-Tracker) Database Transfer to New Mark 43 RMS
description: The USPP has a requirement to transfer the data residing within the Evidence Tracker (E-Tracker) System database to the new Mark 43 Law Enforcement Resource Management System (RMS). Prior to the deployment of the new Mark 43 RMS, the USPP maintained its evidence database on the E-Tracker System. Since the E-Tracker is a proprietary system, the USPP needs a contract to assist in the transfer of the data.

title: FirstNet Authority Broadband Network Subscriptions
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement to establish services using FirstNet Authority which is a nationwide broadband network dedicated exclusively for public safety use, providing a secure, reliable, high-speed network, which offers a suite of voice, data and video streaming push to talk capabilities, so law enforcement officers can talk and share data more efficiently. FirstNet offers vetted and secured law enforcement apps, along with dedicated deployable assets for major events, etc.

title: Harley Davidson Electra Glide Police Motorcycles for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement for a lifecycle replacement of five Harley Davidson Electra Glide Police Motorcycles for its USPP Motors Unit. The USPP Motors Unit enhances public safety and traffic enforcement through proactive patrol and rapid response capabilities. The USPP Motors Unit strives to reduce accidents, promote roadway safety, and provide reliable escorts and dignitary protection.

title: Installation of a Data Circuit to Support USPP Training at the FLETC Cheltenham
description: The USPP has a requirement to install a data circuit to support USPP training requirements at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC) facility located in Cheltenham, MD. The data circuit will be installed at FLETC Cheltenham's Building 1 and will be used to provide sufficient bandwidth to support all the USPP's training of its new officers. FLETC Cheltenham does not have insufficient bandwidth to support USPP's requirements.

title: Installation of a Fence with Gate to Protect the Generator, Radio Tower, and HVAC System at USPP NYFO
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) has a requirement to install a fence with a gate to protect the generator, radio tower, and HVAC system at the USPP NYFO. The installation of a fence will help protect this vital equipment from tampering or vandalism by the public.

title: Lifecycle Replacement of Duty Rifles for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement to conduct a lifecycle replacement of obsolete rifles in support of the mission of USPP officers. The intent of the contract would be to purchase from a family of 5.56 x 45mm semi-automatic duty rifles, replacement parts, and armorer training.

title: Lifecycle Replacement of Level 1 Civil Disturbance Unit (CDU) Equipment for US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement to purchase lifecycle replacement of various Level 1 Civil Disturbance Unit (CDU) equipment and supplies designed to assist law enforcement agencies maintain public safety during protests and riots.

title: LiveScan Cabinet Fingerprint/Palmprint Systems for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement to purchase at least two replacement IDEMIA LiveScan Cabinet Tenprint/Palmprint Systems with compatible color printers for USPP District Stations. The IDEMIA LiveScan System is used to capture biometric data for law enforcement purposes. The IDEMIA LiveScan System supports multi-modal biometric data capture and enrollment including fingerprints, palm prints, and facial images and interacts with the Washington, DC Metropolitan Police Department.

title: Marine Buoys and Fenders for the USPP NYFO Marine Patrol Unit
description: The US Park Police (USPP) New York Field Office (NYFO) Marine Patrol Unit (MPU) has a requirement to purchase marine buoys and fenders which are crucial for protecting boats and ensuring safe docking. Fenders are cushions that protect boats from damage caused by docks or other vessels. Buoys are floating devices used for navigation and mooring, marking key locations in the water.

title: Mobile Command Vehicle for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement for an updated law enforcement mobile command vehicle to serve as a centralized hub for coordination, communication, and decision-making during emergencies and significant major events. These vehicles are equipped with advance technology and communication systems, providing a secure and comfortable environment for command personnel, facilitating real time communication among various agencies.

title: Mobile Data Terminal Pedestals, Vehicle Mounts and Docking Stations for USPP LE Vehicles

title: Next Generation 911 System for the US Park Police
description: The US Park Police (USPP) has a requirement for a Next Generation 911 (NG911) digital, internet protocol (IP) based system that will replace the analog 911 system currently being used in its USPP Dispatch Operations Centers (DOCs). It will enhance emergency number services to create a faster, more resilient system that allows voice, photos, videos, and text message to flow seamlessly from the public to the 911 network. Efforts to acquire the NG911 will involve coordination with DoT and 911.gov

title: Night Vision Goggles for US Park Police SWAT Operations

title: Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) for the US Park Police

title: Purchase and Installation of PIT Equipment on Selected USPP LE Vehicles

A PIT maneuver is a law enforcement pursuit tactic in which a pursuing vehicle suddenly laterally strikes the side-rear of the pursued vehicle, thus causing the pursued vehicle to swing around and come to an unplanned stop.

RADAR uses radio detection and ranging while LIDAR uses laser light detection and ranging which is more precise. The purchase of handheld and dash-mounted RADAR and LIDAR systems will be used in the USPP's execution of EO 14252 and 14333.
